evidence: Vault-root creation/resolution/stat failures and records-directory creation/stat failures are now translated to stable SecretAccessDenied or SecretUnavailable outcomes. Root-as-file, records-as-file, and simulated unavailable-authority tests invoke both put and lease and prove every existing authority/protected byte remains unchanged.

The prior authenticated DPAPI/XChaCha20-Poly1305 record behavior, cross-process CAS, object-key restart, leakage scans, audit denial, and ciphertext-retained corruption recovery remain covered by the exact affected union and immutable initial full security-local report.

The new authority regression deterministically covers both material filesystem-invalid conditions and a PermissionError boundary for both public operations, checking bounded exception types and byte preservation.

The new production-audit regression uses the default sink, not an injected collector. It requires the exact event, level, timestamp, operation, outcome, reason, audit context, opaque reference token, calling capability, and purpose projection for put and lease while scanning the serialized diagnostics for the secret, subject, and name.

SecretAuditEvent and the default Core logging authority now retain the calling capability and declared purpose alongside the ADR-approved operation/outcome/reason/context/opaque-reference fields. Each newly allowed log field has a closed validator; arbitrary token, content, credential, and secret fields remain redacted.

ADR-0017, the architecture guide, security contract README, strict profile/schema, and contract tests now state the same attributed content-safe audit projection. No secret scope identifier or value was added to diagnostics, contracts, databases, exports, support bundles, process arguments, or paths.
No unrelated S04 rotation/recovery/privacy/SQLCipher work, UI reference, migration, provider connector, cloud behavior, or platform adapter was introduced.
